locus: §4.2 — “The spread is the finding, not noise”
current:
The spread is the finding, not noise around a mean. A random-effects fit
across the twenty chambers (logit-scale τ = 0.56, I² = 0.78 — 78% of the
observed between-chamber variance is true heterogeneity, not sampling
noise) puts the chambers' rates at **4.3% to 18.3%, a better-than-fourfold
range**, after every chamber is pulled toward the pool in proportion to
its own noise. The per-chamber table reports the raw estimates; the
shrunken range is the honest spread claim, since the extremes of twenty
noisy cells overstate their own separation (the raw-extremes version is
retired to Appendix B). What drives a chamber's position is not
established here — even two chambers of one legislature can sit far apart
(Appendix C item 7), and the study does not attribute the between-chamber differences to
any measured cause.
proposed:
Between-chamber variation is a result, not merely noise around the pooled
mean. In a random-effects fit across the twenty chambers, logit-scale τ =
0.56 and I² = 0.78, attributing 78% of the observed between-chamber variance
to heterogeneity rather than sampling noise. After each estimate is shrunk
toward the pool in proportion to its uncertainty, chamber rates span **4.3%
to 18.3%, a better-than-fourfold range**. The table reports raw estimates;
the shrunken range supports the spread claim without treating the noisiest
extremes among twenty cells as exact (the raw-extremes version is in Appendix
B). The analysis does not establish what drives a chamber's position or
attribute the differences to any measured cause. Even the two chambers of one
legislature can sit far apart (Appendix C item 7).
rationale: The revision replaces “true heterogeneity” and “honest spread” with standard random-effects language and makes the distinction between raw and shrunken estimates easier to follow. It keeps the causal limit prominent and all statistics unchanged.
